configurePresets.name: native-asan
configurePresets.displayName: Native with address and UB sanitizers
configurePresets.description: vptr is excluded because it needs RTTI and the core is built -fno-rtti (ADR 0012): left on it reports every GoogleTest dispatch as invalid and buries a real finding. Recovery is off so undefined behaviour fails the run instead of printing and passing. float-cast-overflow is named explicitly because GCC leaves it out of -fsanitize=undefined while Clang includes it: this core turns doubles from JavaScript and from platform ports into integers, so the one class of undefined behaviour the boundary is most likely to produce was the one this job could not see.

configurePresets.name: native-contracting
configurePresets.displayName: Native, clang, optimised with fused floating point — the build the debug preset cannot stand in for
configurePresets.description: At -O0 every evaluation of an expression is compiled the same way, so rounding differences between compiled copies cannot show. Optimised with -ffp-contract=fast, the compiler chose per copy whether to fuse multiply-adds or vectorise: before Norm was fused by hand, the gate's copy of the sum of squares became a scalar fused chain and Normalize's a vectorised multiply with plain adds, and near either end of the admissible range they disagreed about whether a quaternion was usable. Rounds 9, 10 and 11 on PR #80 each found a caller shipped with that defect, visible only on such a build. clang because it is the compiler measured doing it; gcc 13 at the same flags produced the same fused chain in every copy. The flags live behind SPHANORAMA_FUSED_ARITHMETIC in CMakeLists.txt, which picks the instruction set per architecture (x86-64-v3 on x86-64, nothing on aarch64) rather than -march=native, which the CI runner's AVX10 CPU turned into a -Werror failure. The CI job checks, through tools/fused_build_check.py, that every compile asked for fast contraction and that the compiler actually fused. OpenCV is off because the question is about the core's own arithmetic.
